Internal helper: the call rebuilt with its variables after the data frame

Source: R/recode.R
dot-jst_vars_dots_line.Rd

The line jconvert() and jdeclare_missing() offer when the variables arrived through vars = in a form that does not run there (Session 355): the call as made, vars = taken out, and the variables listed bare straight after the data frame – the house form, jconvert(d, A, B, to = "stata", modify = TRUE). Every other argument is kept as typed. A data frame given as an expression is named first (mydata <- mk()), as every offered line names it (S343).

Usage

.jst_vars_dots_line(mc, fn, vars, as_c = FALSE, force = NULL)

Arguments

mc

The call, from match.call() in the exported function.

fn

The function's name.

vars

Character; the variables, in the order they go in.

as_c

Logical; the variables as one c().

force

Named character; arguments set on the line, replacing the call's own (c(modify = "TRUE")).

Value

A list: pre ("" or the naming line with its newline), line (the call, indented), and framed (TRUE when the call named its data frame).

Details

jrelabel() (Session 378) takes its list in one slot, as a c(): as_c = TRUE gives the variables as one c() (one name bare) and drops the call's own var; force sets arguments the line must carry – its list form runs only with modify = TRUE, so the line carries it (ruling R23: no line that stops next).
